subject: use dcast to reformat data table without using an aggregate function

messages.author: ea99f640d3869c3c
messages.subject: use dcast to reformat data table without using an aggregate function
parts:
I am trying to cast a dataset from a long format into a wide format,
but I do not want to aggregate the data with a sum or length or any
other function.
I want to return the actual value for each variable.
I tried using the following code:

head(M1)
Well Addition Column Row BarCode Max Min MaxMin Concentration
value
1 A1 1 1 A J00AM5B 140 -7 147 5.00e-05
-2.393567
2 A10 1 10 A J00AM5B 52 -239 291 7.62e-09
3.007783
3 A11 1 11 A J00AM5B 62 -221 283 2.54e-09
2.707708
4 A12 1 12 A J00AM5B 45 -297 342 8.47e-10
4.920761
5 A13 1 13 A J00AM5B 1046 -86 1132 5.00e-05
34.553170
6 A14 1 14 A J00AM5B 1150 -37 1187 1.67e-05
36.616185

q = cast(subset(M1, Addition=="1"), BarCode+Row~Concentration,
fun.aggregate=function(x)x)

I used to be able to do something like this with reshape, but now I
get the following error

Error in vapply(indices, fun, .default) : values must be length 0,
but FUN(X[[1]]) result is length 2

Any help would be greatly appreciatetd

Dan Gillie

messages.author: 9ff02ee016b8a9e0
messages.subject: Re: use dcast to reformat data table without using an aggregate function
parts:
Here is an:

dataset <- data.frame(var1 = rep(c("a","b","c","d","e","f"), each = 2), var2 = rep(c("level1","level2"), 6), value1 = rep(1:12), value2 = rep(13:24))

dcast(melt(dataset), id.var = c("var1","var2","variable"), var1 ~ var2 + variable)


perhaps you can just use recast though...

HTH, Scott
